publicationRule: These subjects are sourced only from official government, prosecution, court or institution records. Charges remain accusations and are never presented as convictions. Power-role status is separately classified and dated.

subjects.legalStatusSummary: Federally charged in April 2026 with possession and production of child sexual abuse material. The accusations remain pending unless and until adjudicated.

findings.title: Federal charges for possession and production of child sexual abuse material
findings.summary: A federal criminal complaint identified Hedgpeth as Hanahan mayor pro tem and a city council member and charged him with possession and production of child sexual abuse material. The charging statement described alleged payments to accounts associated with minors or suspected of selling content.
findings.sourceLabel: District of South Carolina charging statement
findings.jurisdiction: United States federal court, District of South Carolina
findings.status: charged; case pending at last official check
findings.outcome: No final adjudication stated in the cited charging record.
findings.rightOfReply: The charges are accusations. Hedgpeth is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty in court.
findings.counterEvidence: The charging document does not establish guilt, and the official source expressly preserves the presumption of innocence.
findings.proofNeeded: Maintain the indictment, court docket, plea or trial outcome, sentencing record if any, and any dismissal or acquittal.
findings.boundary: Limited to the allegations in the cited federal charging record. A charge is not proof of guilt.

conclusion.finding: The official record establishes a child-exploitation prosecution involving a person who held municipal legislative and mayor-pro-tem authority when charged, followed by a documented vacancy in that council seat.
conclusion.whyItMatters: The case tests whether public institutions rapidly separate active authority from a serious pending safeguarding prosecution while preserving due process.
conclusion.mechanism: The alleged conduct involved online access and payments; the public-power relevance comes from the separately documented municipal office.
conclusion.effect: Strengthens the need for current/former status tracking and charge-versus-conviction separation.
conclusion.widerDirection: Track court disposition, municipal ethics and vacancy procedures, and whether public access or systems played any documented role.
conclusion.alternativeExplanation: The allegations may be contested or disproved; a vacant seat does not establish guilt.
conclusion.doesNotProve: It does not prove guilt, institutional knowledge, facilitation by colleagues, or wrongdoing by the City of Hanahan.
conclusion.evidenceStrength: E4 official federal charge plus official city vacancy evidence
conclusion.confidence: high for charge and former-role status; no conclusion on guilt

powerRoles.organization: Local university and other colleges or universities identified generally in the official record

findings.title: Federal conviction and 222-month sentence for attempted child enticement and CSAM offenses
findings.summary: After a stipulated bench trial, Githens was found guilty of attempted enticement of a minor and receipt and distribution of child sexual abuse material. In July 2026 the court sentenced him to 222 months in prison and ten years of supervised release.
findings.sourceLabel: Eastern District of California sentencing statement
findings.jurisdiction: United States federal court, Eastern District of California
findings.outcome: 222 months in prison, ten years of supervised release, registration requirements and financial penalties stated by DOJ.
victims: fictional seven-year-old presented by an undercover agent
findings.rightOfReply: Githens exercised trial rights through a stipulated bench trial and retains applicable appellate rights.
findings.counterEvidence: The enticement count involved an undercover operation and a fictional child, while the separate CSAM offenses involved actual abusive material. The conviction does not implicate students, colleagues or institutions without separate evidence.
findings.proofNeeded: Maintain the judgment, restitution determination and final appellate status.
findings.boundary: Limited to the exact offenses, defendant, court, jurisdiction and disposition in the cited final record.

conclusion.finding: The final federal record establishes child-exploitation offenses committed by a person who previously held educational authority and consulting access in higher education.
conclusion.whyItMatters: Educational authority can create trust and access, but the cited case does not state that institutional systems or students were used in the offenses.
conclusion.mechanism: The proven conduct involved online communications and child sexual abuse material rather than a documented institutional channel.
conclusion.effect: Strengthens the education-sector accountability lane while preserving the boundary between personal offending and institutional responsibility.
conclusion.widerDirection: Check whether employers received warnings, conducted reviews or changed safeguarding controls, but publish only documented findings.
conclusion.alternativeExplanation: The offenses may have been entirely outside his professional roles; the cited record does not establish institutional facilitation.
conclusion.doesNotProve: It does not prove abuse of students, knowledge by colleagues or wrongdoing by any university or client institution.
conclusion.evidenceStrength: E6 final federal conviction and sentence
